correctness.rationale: Under the i.i.d. atomless assumption the ranks form a uniform permutation. For i<j the prefixes and suffixes used by the flags are disjoint. For i=j the joint probability is the beta integral, and the truncated pivot is strictly stochastically smaller than uniform if i>1, giving strict negative covariance if also i<n. The endpoint flags A_1 and B_n are constants. For i>j, after conditioning on A_i, the pivot M has Beta(1,i) law, and the j-through-(i-1) maximum is M+(1-M)Z with independent Z~Beta(i-j,1). Its argmax is uniform in that block and the n-i subsequent draws are independent. Thus the conditional probability of B_j is at least 1/(n-j), strictly above 1/(n-j+1), even when i=n; expansion and beta moments give exactly the displayed factorial sum. For the shifted matrix, deleting row k and column j in a leading k-minor leaves a block triangular minor with factors D_(j-1) and the superdiagonal h_(t,t+1), j<=t<k. Their signs cancel the cofactor sign, so every term in the last-row recurrence is positive, including the 1x1 case. This proves sign-nonsingularity, not just nonsingularity of one numerical matrix.
residual_risks: The replay is finite; the beta-moment argument and cofactor decomposition establish the universal claims. The covariance assertion is linear and assumes no ties.

value.rationale: These are two classical and naturally paired record processes. Position indexing exposes a directional pattern of exact independence, negative shared-pivot dependence and positive separated-pivot overlap that joint counts suppress. The sign pattern rules out any nonzero linear contrast invisible to all reverse records and gives robustness without estimating determinant magnitudes. This is a useful finite-size dependence law, not just a single enumerated determinant.
residual_risks: No claim about higher-order independence, recovery of one record set from the other, or robustness to ties and non-identical sampling.
